title: For which n do planar crescent configurations exist?

fields.Problem description: Determine the integers $n \ge 2$ for which a set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, with no three collinear and no four concyclic, realizes exactly $n-1$ distinct distances whose multiplicities are $1,2,\ldots,n-1$, each occurring once. Multiplicity counts unordered pairs of distinct points; the distances need not be ordered by size. Such a set is called a crescent configuration. Erdős conjectured that no such configurations exist for all sufficiently large $n$.
fields.Publication details:
[Erdős Problem #217](https://www.erdosproblems.com/217) — problem statement and historical references.
Burt et al., [Crescent configurations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.07220) — arXiv:1509.07220 (2015), definitions of general position and crescent configurations.
Fish et al., [Crescent configurations in normed spaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08769) — arXiv:1909.08769 (2019), Section 1.1, the Euclidean formulation and its general-position restrictions.

review_notes.label: Complete solution and Lean evidence · Source review 2026-10-08
review_notes.note: Resolves the asymptotic shortest-expansion question (Erdős #304): the maximum, over 1 ≤ a < b, of the minimum number of distinct positive unit fractions representing a/b is Θ(log log b). This does not assert an exact minimum formula for each individual rational. Source references are fixed at commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. This entry records the published complete-result claim and accompanying formalization; independent mathematical review, a clean Lean build, transitive axiom audit and Comparator execution have not been performed in this catalog update. The catalog eligibility flag is Yes; both claim roles are Unclaimed because neither role is registered in candidates or awards. Independent verification remains outstanding.

review_notes.label: Record correction · Source review 2026-09-13
review_notes.note: Disproved: 12167 = 23³ and 12168 = 2³ × 3² × 13² are consecutive powerful numbers, and neither is a perfect square. A powerful number has exponent at least two in every prime factor. The displayed factorizations verify this property for 12167 and 12168. Both lie strictly between 110² = 12100 and 111² = 12321, so neither is a square. This disproves the stated yes/no question. This record covers that question only, not the separate counting question in [Erdős problem #365](https://www.erdosproblems.com/365). The previous 1976→2026 interval is removed because it does not establish the duration of the stated question.

review_notes.label: Complete solution and Lean evidence · Source review 2026-10-08
review_notes.note: Resolves the cycle–clique Ramsey conjecture for its stated parameter range: R(C_m,K_n) = (m−1)(n−1)+1 for m ≥ n ≥ 3 except (3,3), where the value is 6. No formula for unrestricted m,n is asserted. Source references are fixed at commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. This entry records the published complete-result claim and accompanying formalization; independent mathematical review, a clean Lean build, transitive axiom audit and Comparator execution have not been performed in this catalog update. The catalog eligibility flag is Yes; both claim roles are Unclaimed because neither role is registered in candidates or awards. Independent verification remains outstanding.

review_notes.label: Complete solution and Lean evidence · Source review 2026-10-08
review_notes.note: Proves the missing logarithmic independence bound α(G) ≥ c_r n log(d)/d for each fixed r ≥ 4 and every finite K_r-free graph of average degree d ≥ 2. The r = 3 case is the established triangle-free result; the new Lean target covers r ≥ 4. Source references are fixed at commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. This entry records the published complete-result claim and accompanying formalization; independent mathematical review, a clean Lean build, transitive axiom audit and Comparator execution have not been performed in this catalog update. The catalog eligibility flag is Yes; both claim roles are Unclaimed because neither role is registered in candidates or awards. Independent verification remains outstanding.

review_notes.label: Complete solution and Lean evidence · Source review 2026-10-08
review_notes.note: Proves the joint Dickman law in ordinary natural density for largest prime factors of consecutive integers: for 0 < a,b < 1 the joint density is ρ(1/a)ρ(1/b), where ρ is the Dickman function. review_notes.label: Complete solution and Lean evidence · Source review 2026-10-08
review_notes.note: Resolves the stated power-free-values conjecture for irreducible integer polynomials of degree d ≥ 4 with k = d−2 and no fixed prime kth-power divisor: k-free values have positive density with the specified local-product main term. No assertion for arbitrary unrelated exponents is made. Source references are fixed at commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. This entry records the published complete-result claim and accompanying formalization; independent mathematical review, a clean Lean build, transitive axiom audit and Comparator execution have not been performed in this catalog update. The catalog eligibility flag is Yes; both claim roles are Unclaimed because neither role is registered in candidates or awards. Independent verification remains outstanding.

title: Chromatic number and minimum order of triangle-free graphs

fields.Date proposed: No later than 1967 for the maximum-chromatic-number formulation; the inverse minimum-order formulation is recorded in a 1971 source.
fields.Problem description: Determine the maximum chromatic number f(n) of a triangle-free graph on n vertices, or inversely the minimum order h₃(k) of a triangle-free graph with chromatic number k. Find precise asymptotics; the minimum-order formulation also asks whether h₃(k+1)/h₃(k) tends to one.
fields.Elapsed years:
**Minimum-order formulation:** About 55 years (since 1971)
**Maximum-chromatic-number formulation:** About 59 years (since 1967)
fields.Problem sources: [Erdős #1013](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1013) and [Erdős #1104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104) explicitly describe h₃ and f as inverse functions. The edge-count variant discussed in #1104 remains a related extension.

review_notes.label: Mathematical solution · Source review 2026-10-08
review_notes.note: Reports that for each fixed dimension d ≥ 3 every n-point set determines at least c_d n^(2/d) distinct distances, matching the order of the lattice construction. This records the higher-dimensional conjecture, not an exact leading constant. The manuscript is pinned at commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`; independent mathematical review has not been performed in this update. No corresponding public Lean proof was located in the supplied fixed-source cross-check. Lean remains No, eligibility remains No and both claim roles remain Unavailable.

review_notes.label: Complete solution and Lean evidence · Source review 2026-10-08
review_notes.note: Disproves the proposed fixed-proportion lower gap: for every η > 0 and every sufficiently large length N, some real sign-coefficient polynomial has maximum modulus on the unit circle at most (1+η)√N. The formalization covers all sufficiently large integer lengths. Source references are fixed at commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. This entry records the published complete-result claim and accompanying formalization; independent mathematical review, a clean Lean build, transitive axiom audit and Comparator execution have not been performed in this catalog update. The catalog eligibility flag is Yes; both claim roles are Unclaimed because neither role is registered in candidates or awards. Independent verification remains outstanding.

title: Mirror symmetry conjecture

fields.Mathematical area: Algebraic geometry / Hodge theory / Symplectic geometry
fields.Problem description: For mirror pairs in the Katzarkov–Kontsevich–Pantev framework, identify the A-model and B-model noncommutative Hodge structures, including Calabi–Yau and Landau–Ginzburg settings.
